title: ProgressionTraide
description: Dynamic trading/workstations that evolve with progression—no more static “one-size” trades.
body:
# ProgressionTraide

Static trades get boring fast. ProgressionTraide brings a trading system that can scale with progression, roles, or server design. That means trading stays interesting, feels earned, and actually supports long-term economy gameplay.

# Highlights:

Progression-aware trading/workstation profiles

Great for profession-based gameplay and evolving economies

Designed for RPG servers where “growth” matters

Perfect for: professions, economy progression, MMO traders.

# Why you’ll love it

Trades don’t get boring after 2 days

Makes professions/economy feel alive and scalable

Supports real progression-based server design

# How to use it

### Typical workflow

Reload trade/workstation configs after edits:

/ptraide reload

List available trade profiles/workstations:

/ptraide list

Open a trade/workstation GUI for a player (admin/testing):

/ptraide open <player> <profile>

Give a player access to a profile (if your setup uses permissions/unlocks):

/ptraide unlock <player> <profile>

Remove access / lock a profile (testing/balancing):

/ptraide lock <player> <profile>

Show a player’s unlocked profiles/status:

/ptraide status <player>

### How it’s used in-game

Players interact with a trader/workstation (NPC/block/GUI entry—depending on your setup).

The plugin selects the correct profile based on progression / tier / role and shows matching trades.

As players progress, new trades unlock or existing offers scale.

If your command names differ, paste your /ptraide help output and I’ll rewrite the command section 100% matching your plugin.

# Features

Progression-aware trade/workstation profiles

Great for profession loops and evolving economies

Designed to integrate with an RPG ecosystem

# Setup

Install the plugin

Configure trade profiles/workstations

Connect to progression logic (tiers/roles if used)

Test and tune scaling

# Compatibility

Platform: Paper / Spigot (Paper recommended)

Best with: Progression + Economy + professions
